texts: good. the bare-plural generic goes to a kind-level claim and the multi-part predicate nominal splits cleanly into a genus plus two property atoms, so nothing is lost.

mixed: the wraith-rise rule itself is right and fires, but "the water of the Sunken Cove" is encoded with the containment head (LocatedIn), which is reserved for a surface "in / at / inside / within" — an of-genitive is supposed to route to the possessive heads instead, and which of those covers a mass constituent of a geographic feature is itself unsettled, so the sentence as written has no clean form. Swapping the preposition licenses exactly the atoms the parser already produced: "Wraiths rise from the water in the Sunken Cove."

good. the adjudicator refuted the reviewer's only objection — the "no other" restriction is carried by a strength-0 rule whose distinctness guard needs that contrast witness — and the fireability check passes. Worth knowing: the excluded water is an anonymous witness minted for this sentence alone, so it carries no link back to the Sunken Cove water of the previous line.

bad: the belief content cannot be recorded as written. "The unsettled dead of the storm-surge" is a definite, PP-restricted predicate nominal, and a kind-level "wraiths are N" has no slot for the of-restrictor, so the parse hangs it on the bare kind and ends up saying — inside the belief — that unsettled-dead-at-large belongs to that storm-surge; the ruling was that no compliant form exists and the whole identification would have to be dropped from the belief. Fold the storm-surge into the kind word and drop the definite article, so the predicate nominal becomes a plain kind plus a plain property — the same shape that works in this item's first sentence: "The Keepers believe that wraiths are unsettled storm-surge dead." One caveat: the definite "the ... dead" reads as an identity (exactly those and no others), which has no carrier either way, so the rewrite records that wraiths are such dead rather than that they are all of them.
